title: Love grows with knowing (10:6)
hook: one loves God according to how much one knows
tomorrow: so what would a plan of return look like on paper?

segments.voice: Yesterday: slowly toward love. Start with reward, then gently, little by little, toward love. Today, what makes the love grow.

A song you skipped the first time can become the one you play on repeat, once you learn the words, catch the bass line under the chorus, find out who it was written for. Can you love what you barely know? Maimonides says not much, and he means it as good news.
screen: `SKIPPED IT THE FIRST TIME.` → `THEN YOU LEARNED THE WORDS.` → `LOVE WHAT YOU BARELY KNOW?`

segments.voice: Here's his line from chapter ten. A person loves the Holy One only by the knowledge with which they know Him. According to the knowing, the love: if little, then little; if much, then much. So, he says, a person should give themselves to understanding the wisdoms that make their Creator known to them, as far as a human can. This surprises people. They expect love and learning to sit at opposite ends: the heart over here, the head over there. Maimonides fuses them. In the very first pages of his law book he says the same: look closely at the world's wonders, and love wakes up. Learning isn't the cold part of faith. It's the fuel. Try it with the senses. A pharmacist can look at a pill most of us couldn't name and tell you what it does, who it helps, what it must never be taken with. A gardener knows a plant by the smell of a crushed leaf. Knowing something that closely isn't cold. It's a kind of care. One honest note: other Jewish teachers, later on, put more weight on the heart's simple devotion, open to the unlearned as much as the scholar. Maimonides stands at the knowing end of that conversation, and the tradition keeps both voices.
screen: `ACCORDING TO THE KNOWING, THE LOVE.` · `LITTLE KNOWING, LITTLE LOVE.` · `LEARNING IS THE FUEL.` · `A KIND OF CARE.` · then, large: `LOVE GROWS WITH KNOWING.`

segments.voice: Pick up one small thing near you: a leaf, a coin, your own hand. For the whole sit, learn it: its edges, its weight, its temperature, one detail you've never noticed before. Let the looking get slower and closer.
Love grows with knowing: Maimonides' rule. Know a little, love a little; know more, love more.
Something to keep: love grows with knowing, and learning is the fuel, not the cold part. Twenty-eight down.
